description: Dairy milk evaporator: two-effect MVR evaporation with milk heat treatment, 247 t/h raw milk (30 t/h milk powder); evaporation system in isolation. Loads in kW.

provenance.data source: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 2.
provenance.stream data: published (Table 2); Table 2 dT_cont used (chiller water 0.5 K; the text's pinch range implies 2.5 K, which leaves the targets unchanged)
provenance.eta_lorenz: published: 50 % exergetic (Carnot) efficiency (Sec. 4.2); reproduces the paper's simple-design COP 2.1
provenance.source_T_C: published: ambient / dead state 15 °C (Sec. 2), the source of the paper's simple design
provenance.sink levels: 105 °C published (simple design, Sec. 4.2.3); the 15-55 °C level is assumed (illustrative, follows the low-temperature part of the GCC)
provenance.basis: ASSUMED for reproduce_secondary_economics.py: 8000 h/year (case basis_hint). Original: none: operating hours not given
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: Stampfli et al. (2018) dairy values, stream mapping assumed
provenance.eta_lorenz_sensitivity: 0.45-0.52: Lorenz (Carnot) efficiencies implied by the DEA catalogue HTHP sheets 2.a/2.b (COP 4.45/2.75/2.4/2.05 at lifts of 40/65/80/100 K), as for the brewery
provenance.COP check: HTHP 105 °C (steam, 90 K lift): COP 2.10 vs DEA sheet 2.a 2.22 at 90 K minus 0.15 for steam = 2.07 (+1.5 %). Warm-water heat pump 15 -> 55 °C: Lorenz COP 7.86 vs DEA sheet 1.1 'up to 60 °C, lift 40 K' 5.33 (+47 %; the Lorenz model credits the full 40 K sink glide, which needs a glide-matched cycle such as transcritical CO2); with COP 5.33 RQ1 falls from 26 % to 23 %
provenance.steam sink: verified: the 105 °C level supplies the Direct Steam Injection that follows the 8 -> 95 °C preheat (Walmsley et al. 2024, Sec. 3.2), so the DEA steam-generation add-on applies

default_sources.electricity_to_gas_ratio: published: Padullés et al. (2026), Sec. 5.2, 'current European ratios of around 2'
default_sources.boiler_efficiency: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat, sheet 6.1 'Boiler, gas and oil' (2025): total efficiency, net, annual average 93.9 % (range 91.9-94.9 %), steam boiler with economiser; converted to the gross (GCV) basis of Eurostat gas prices with NCV/GCV = 0.90: 0.939 x 0.90 = 0.845. Earlier default 0.817 (US DOE Steam Tip Sheet #15, HHV) kept as sensitivity
default_sources.payback_threshold_years: research question 1 (industry practice 3-5 years: Cooremans, cited in Padullés et al. 2026)
default_sources.gas_EF_kg_per_kWh: IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2, Ch. 2, Table 2.2: natural gas, stationary combustion, 56,100 kg CO2/TJ (NCV) = 0.202 kg/kWh NCV = 0.182 kg/kWh GCV (NCV/GCV = 0.90), direct combustion only, matching the scope of production-based grid factors. Padullés et al. (2026, Sec. 5.3) use 0.219 (scope not stated); report it as a sensitivity
default_sources.grid_EF_kg_per_kWh: APA, 'Fator de Emissão da Eletricidade - 2025', Table T1: Portugal 2023, 0.107 t CO2eq/MWh (annual, production-based, direct emissions). Sensitivities: mainland 2023 0.092; 5-year moving average 0.167 (Table T2); Electricity Maps 2025 flow-traced 0.1172
default_sources.co2_price_EUR_per_t: 0 by default (site may be outside the EU ETS); sensitivity uses the EUA price
default_sources.pef_gas: convention: primary energy of a fuel = its final energy, on the net calorific value (NCV) basis of energy statistics
default_sources.gas_ncv_over_gcv: IPCC (1996) Revised Guidelines, Reference Manual, Ch. 1, Table 1-4 note a: GCV-NCV 10 % for natural gas. Gas is bought on GCV (Regulation (EU) 2016/1952); primary energy is counted on NCV, the basis of the EU primary-energy factors (Directive 2012/27/EU Annex IV; supervisor review B5)
default_sources.refrigeration_credit_fraction: share of the refrigeration that the heat pump sources can take over that is actually credited (1 = all, continuous operation as in Padullés et al. 2026 Sec. 5.1; lower values represent batch mismatch between heat pump and cooling loads)
default_sources.boiler_variable_om_EUR_per_MWh: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat, sheet 6.1 'Boiler, gas and oil' (2025): variable O&M 1.23 EUR/MWh of heat, avoided with the gas heat it no longer supplies. The fixed O&M (2,000 EUR/MW/y) is not credited: the boiler is kept as back-up

case_sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands: gas I3 0.0512, I4 0.0445, I5 0.0420; electricity ID 0.1135, IE 0.0897, IF 0.0789. Band check at 8000 h/year, site level (the site buys the energy): Walmsley et al. (2016), 'Total Site Utility Systems Optimisation for Milk Powder Production', CET 52, 235-240, DOI 10.3303/CET1652040: 30 t/h milk powder plant, electricity 210-220 kWh/t powder (literature 150-400), fuel 5,200 MJ/t powder (base case), and Walmsley et al. (2024): this evaporator belongs to a 30 t/h plant. Gas 5.2 GJ/t x 30 t/h x 8000 h = 1.25 million GJ (I5); electricity 220 kWh/t x 30 x 8000 = 52.8 GWh + heat pumps 11.7 GWh (IE). I4 below 6,400 h/year. Borderline gas band: the 5.2 GJ/t is the base-case fuel use; the improved design in the same paper (Table 1, design 1.0: 3.66 GJ/t thermal) gives 0.88 million GJ at 8000 h, band I4 (0.0445)
case_sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base
case_sources.chiller_cop: Sinnott and Towler (2020), Sec. 6.4.4, Eq. 6.20: real COP about 0.6 x Carnot (as for the brewery). Evaporator: chilled water leaves at 4 °C (Walmsley et al. 2024, Table 2) minus 5 K refrigerated-brine approach (Sec. 12.7.3: 3-5 K) = -1 °C; condenser 30 °C (ambient 15 °C + 10 K cooling-water rise + 5 K approach): 0.6 x 272.15/31 = 5.27. Q̇c,min (456 kW) is entirely this chilled-water load

grass_roots_reference._definition: grass-roots reference, not the answer to RQ1 or RQ3: heat pump heat / Q̇h,min for a site already recovering heat at the energy target. RQ1-RQ3 against today's site: consolidate_rq.py

grass_roots_sensitivities.basis: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025): indirect cost of new hot-water piping added to each heat pump class (scenario)

retrofit_bounds.baseline_meaning: the source describes a heat-integrated plant whose exchangers are not published: the lower bound ('already at target') is the realistic estimate; 'no heat recovery' greatly overstates the savings
retrofit_bounds.note: Walmsley et al. (2024), Sec. 3.2 and Fig. 4: the base case derives from the heat-integrated 'ultra-low energy' design of Walmsley et al. (2018, Energy 146, 67-81) and the raw milk is preheated 8 -> 95 °C by heat recovery, but the exchangers are not listed. Use the lower bound; the exact existing network may be in Walmsley et al. (2018)

new_heat_recovery_network.cost_law: Towler 2020 plate and frame (304 SS) x 3.5 (Hand factor, installed)

options.option: New heat recovery at target + heat pumps
Lower bound: plant already at target, heat pumps only

assumptions.new network: area target (Bath formula, case film coefficients) and units target at the case's temperature shifts, costed per unit with the cost law
assumptions.heat pumps: case sink levels; on the no-recovery plant they are sized on the network-constrained stream set (no process-to-process transfer)

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: Stampfli et al. (2018), CET 70, 901-906, Table 1 (dairy plant): liquid product 500, water 2,000, evaporation/condensation 5,000 W/(m2 K). Mapping to these streams is our assumption: water for chiller water, CIP, direct-use water and cow water (milk condensate); product for raw milk and concentrate; condensation for vapour bleed, condenser and flash vapours

RQ2.cost_law: Towler 2020 plate and frame (304 SS), bare (F = 1)
Towler 2020 plate and frame (304 SS) x 3.5 (Hand factor, installed)
